transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Time: 10:00am PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sanjay Patel (BrightPath - Head of ML), Aisha Khan (BrightPath - Platform), Tom Lee (BrightPath - Security), Leah Morgan (BrightPath - Product)

---
Summary (auto): Reviewed model perf and decided next steps: Diego to run int8 vs fp16 benches with real prompts; Maya to send pricing and security pack; BrightPath to provide sample prompts and verify success criteria.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick roll call?
[00:06] Sanjay: yep, Sanjay here, Aisha?
[00:08] Aisha: Aisha on the call.
[00:10] Tom: Tom here.
[00:12] Diego: Diego from Redwood.
[00:14] Leah: Leah.
[00:15] Maya: Cool, thanks. quick agenda: run through the updated benchmarks Diego put in the sheet, talk model selection and pinning for pilot, then security/VPC ask, and wrap with action items. sound good?
[00:25] Sanjay: sounds good. we skimmed the sheet this morning — some numbers looked promising but a few q's on tokenization differences.
[00:32] Diego: yeah, i'll start with the benchmark updates. note these were run on our hosted infrastructure with batching sim that matches your traffic profile: 90th p50-ish latencies in the doc. i also added a int8 run but it's preliminary.
[00:45] Diego: so for the 13B family the fp16 throughput was about 380 tokens/sec single inst, int8 bumped throughput to 610 tokens/sec but we saw small quality diffs on the long-form summaries around instruction-following.
[01:05] Sanjay: when you say small diffs, can you quantify? rouge or something analog?
[01:10] Diego: qualitative right now — a couple of hallucinated clinical names on one prompt. i'll extract exact examples and add a delta column.
[01:20] Leah: hm that's important for us — hallucination on patient-like entities is a blocker.
[01:25] Tom: agreed — and we need to keep the PII safe. we're planning to keep everything anonymized but also want to validate redwood's redaction and KMS options.
[01:35] Maya: on that note, i'll attach our compliance pack and SOC2 snapshot after the call — there's also a short questionnaire you asked for, i'll fill that and send next.
[01:45] Aisha: thanks Maya. on model selection, sanjay prefers the 13B latency profile but also wants fallback. what's the recommended pinning strategy?
[01:55] Diego: our suggestion for pilot: pin to a curated 13B variant (we used rwd-13b-v2 in the bench) for normal traffic, and configure an automatic fallback to a cheaper but compatible model when capacity/noisy neighbor issues happen or when latency SLO would be violated. you can also pin a quantized variant if you accept slight quality tradeoffs.
[02:20] Sanjay: and how easy is rollback if we see regressions post-deploy?
[02:25] Diego: rollbacks are straightforward — the console supports quick rollbacks per route. the tricky part is ensuring the cache/KV state is compatible; we recommend a canary traffic split and a short overlap window where both versions serve to warm the KV cache.
[02:40] Sanjay: ok that sounds doable. Leah, product side — does warm cache matter for your UX timelines?
[02:45] Leah: yes, user-facing latency spikes will be really visible; we want minimal cold-starts. so warming strategy + gradual rollout is preferred.
[02:55] Aisha: one operational Q — if we go Hosted for the pilot and Dedicated later, can we keep the same model pin config?
[03:02] Maya: yes, that's a core Redwood feature — the API/config is consistent across hosted and dedicated. you'll be able to pin the same model identifier, just the underlying infra changes.
[03:12] Tom: security — when you say "same config" does that require us to rekey or anything when moving to dedicated VPC?
[03:18] Diego: no rekey required necessarily; we support customer-managed KMS. if you bring your own keys we'll need to coordinate policies, but secrets stay intact.
[03:28] Tom: ok good. Leah: back to the bench numbers — can you share more on the prompt set used?
[03:33] Diego: the sheet used a 500-prompt sample from public demos plus a curated clinical subset of about 120 prompts. we can re-run with your 1k sample for more fidelity.
[03:42] Sanjay: we'll prep that — can you run both fp16 and int8 against it?
[03:46] Diego: yes, i'll run both, and i'll also include a low-latency config that reduces batch window for p50 optimization.
[03:55] Maya: when you run int8, please flag any hallucination examples and include the output tokens so sanjay can inspect.
[04:02] Diego: will do.
[04:05] Sanjay: pricing — rough ask: cost delta between pinned 13B hosted vs dedicated with reserved capacity for steady traffic?
[04:12] Maya: i'll send a pricing matrix after the call, but ballpark: hosted per-token will be higher at low volume; dedicated reserved capacity amortizes at your commit and will be cheaper per token at scale. i'll include pilot credits to make the initial tests economical.
[04:25] Aisha: and is there an SLA for dedicated?
[04:28] Maya: yes, dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. details in the doc i'll share.
[04:33] Tom: can you share audit logs / tracing for requests? we need to show per-route access in our audits.
[04:38] Diego: we have token-level tracing and per-model request logs, retention options are configurable (and add-on for longer retention).
[04:46] Sanjay: competitor check — any measurable perf delta versus OpenAI gpt-4o-mini or Vertex for the same prompt set?
[04:54] Diego: in our internal benchmarks the rwd-13b-v2 matches gpt-4o-mini for many retrieval+instruction tasks at lower cost; i'll add column comparisons in the sheet but caveat: cross-vendor benching noisy due to infra differences.
[05:10] Leah: okay, sounds good. one more question about fallback: if pinned model returns degraded outputs, can we auto-fallback to an earlier version rather than a smaller model?
[05:18] Diego: yes, you can define fallback policies: version-based fallback (rollback to last stable) or model-family-based fallback (drop to smaller model). you can also chain fallbacks.
[05:28] Sanjay: what's the monitoring threshold you recommend to trigger auto-fallback?
[05:32] Diego: typically a combination: error-rate > X% (we suggest 2-3%) OR p95 latency above configured SLO for N minutes. we can share default policies and you can tune.
[05:45] Tom: also need to ensure that fallback events are alerted to our on-call. can we push alerts to our pager?
[05:51] Maya: yes alerts integrate with PagerDuty/Slack/Teams. we'll include the alerting docs.
[05:58] [07:00] (technical aside) Diego: about KV cache compatibility — if you move between architectures or quant levels the cache keys might differ. recommended practice: when rolling between major model variants, do a cache warm by routing a small % of traffic to the new version first.
[07:20] Sanjay: understood. we will prefer staged rollouts.
[07:25] Maya: quick note — i've uploaded a link to the compliance pack: https://redwood.example.com/compliance/brightpath-2026-05. also benchmark sheet: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/brightpath-pilot-2026-05-05 (diego will add int8 runs there).
[07:42] Aisha: good, will check.
[07:45] Leah: regarding evaluation, we want both automated metrics and manual review for the initial 200 outputs. can we annotate outputs in the console?
[07:53] Diego: we have an eval harness you can use; i'll show a quick demo next week. annotations and tagging are supported.
[08:00] Sanjay: timeline — we aim to have pilot results in two weeks, then decide whether to move to dedicated in June.
[08:08] Maya: fits with our timeline.
[08:10] Tom: one more security Q — if we do on-prem/private later, any changes in model pinning semantics?
[08:16] Diego: no, same semantics. private deployment just changes control plane and network posture, but model identifiers and rollout APIs stay the same.
[08:24] Sanjay: great. any blockers for you all?
[08:28] Aisha: we need the infra checklist — VPC peering, subnets, egress policies.
[08:32] Maya: i'll send infra checklist and propose a working session with Aisha & Tom next tuesday.
[08:40] Sanjay: and we'll provide the 1k sample prompts by Sunday.
[08:44] Maya: perfect.
[08:46] Diego: i'll start the int8 runs tonight and aim to have results by Tues.
[08:50] Leah: thanks everyone.
[08:52] Maya: recap of action items: (1) Diego bench fp16/int8 + flag hallucination examples, (2) Maya send pricing + SOC2 + infra checklist, (3) Sanjay provide prompt set and success criteria. meet next week same time for results review.
[09:10] Tom: thanks all.
[09:12] End call.
